stem: Monitoring counts fall after an IPM action, but the second scouting round inspects only half as many plants and sites. Why is the result uncertain?
choices: The sampling method changed, so the lower observed count may reflect reduced observation effort rather than a real change in pressure
The lower count can be accepted because the management action occurred before the second round, even though fewer locations were inspected
The lower count most likely reflects movement within the room, so reduced scouting effort has little effect on interpreting the trend
The rounds remain directly comparable because they occurred in the same room, which provides enough consistency for trend interpretation
rationale: Outcome verification requires comparable monitoring effort. When sampling intensity changes, an apparent reduction can come from the measurement process instead of a true change in pest pressure.
